svg.title: Three producer settings, three measured tradeoffs
svg.desc: Left panel: acks bar chart -- acks=0 measured at 4442 messages per second (waits for nothing), acks=1 at 4182 messages per second (waits for the leader broker), acks=all at 3405 messages per second (waits for every in-sync replica) -- throughput drops as the durability guarantee gets stronger. Right panel: batching bar chart -- a tiny batch size of 200 bytes with no linger measured at 3369 messages per second, versus a large batch size of 1 megabyte with 20 milliseconds of linger measured at 17911 messages per second, a 5.3x gap. A note below states compression traded CPU time for an 89.6% reduction in bytes on a real batch of trip events.
svg.text: 3405 msg/s -- waits for every in-sync replica
23% less throughput for acks='all' -- the only one that survives a broker failing right after the write.
Batching: linger.ms and batch.size vs. throughput
3369 msg/s -- near one request per message
Bigger batches, a short wait to fill them -- far fewer network requests for the same 3000 messages.
Compression traded CPU time for an 89.6% reduction in bytes sent, measured on a real batch of 150 trip events (gzip).
